scope: Public pages + data exposure (logged-out user view). Confirms/refutes 5 prior findings + adds new.

findings.title: Public /api/v1/providers/:type and /:type/:id return FULL DB rows (userId, GST, commission, aadhaarVerified, availability) to logged-out users with no field projection
findings.evidence:
providers.ts route has NO auth preHandler on the GETs:
  server.get('/:type', async (request, reply) => { ... const result = await providerService.getProviders(canonicalType, {...}); return result; });   // line 61
  server.get('/:type/:id', async (request, reply) => { ... const provider = await providerService.getProviderById(canonicalType, id); ... return { provider }; });  // line 94

provider.service.ts queryProviders list call has no `select` (full row returned):
  prisma.panditProfile.findMany({ where, skip, take: limit, orderBy })   // line 367
  prisma.storeProfile.findMany({ where, skip, take: limit, orderBy })    // line 377
  prisma.astrologerProfile.findMany({ where, skip, take: limit, orderBy }) // line 396

enrichRatingFields spreads the ENTIRE raw row and explicitly re-adds aadhaarVerified:
  return { ...p, ratingAvg, ratingCount, aadhaarVerified: typeof p.aadhaarVerified === 'boolean' ? p.aadhaarVerified : false };  // lines 229-234

queryProviderById detail call uses findUnique with NO select AND NO approved filter:
  return (await prisma.panditProfile.findUnique({ where: { id } })) as unknown as Record<string, unknown> | null;  // line 454 (same pattern 455-464 for all 6 types)

Web client consumes the leaked fields (proves end-to-end leak DB->API->SSR):
  export interface ApprovedProvider { id: string; userId: string; ... aadhaarVerified?: boolean; ... }  // apps/web/lib/api.ts:410-419
findings.impact: Any anonymous visitor can enumerate approved providers and read internal/private columns: userId (UUID user handle -> enables cross-endpoint user correlation), StoreProfile.gstNumber (GSTIN, business tax ID), StoreProfile.commission (0.20 Decimal platform take-rate, business-secret), PanditProfile.aadhaarVerified + AstrologerProfile/PanditProfile.availability (weekly schedule blob), plus internal moderation state approved/approvedAt. The web client ApprovedProvider interface confirms userId + aadhaarVerified are actually consumed downstream. The DETAIL endpoint (/providers/:type/:id) is worse: queryProviderById has NO `approved: true` filter (unlike the list which sets where={approved:true} at line 327), so an attacker who guesses or obtains any provider UUID can read the full row of UNAPPROVED/pending/rejected providers too (PII of applicants not yet public).
findings.repro: curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/providers/store' (no auth) -> each item contains userId, gstNumber, commission. curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/providers/pandit/<any-pandit-uuid>' -> response.provider contains userId, aadhaarVerified, availability, approved, approvedAt even if approved=false.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit `select` to every findMany/findUnique in queryProviders/queryProviderById mirroring priests-public.ts (lines 122-133): exclude userId, gstNumber, commission, aadhaarVerified, availability, approved, approvedAt. Add `approved: true` to queryProviderById's where (use findFirst with where:{id, approved:true} instead of findUnique). Alternatively run the result through a whitelist serializer before reply.send. Do NOT rely on the client to ignore fields.

findings.title: Temple public list/search/nearby/detail expose internal trustScore (and detail leaks phone/email/streamUrl/status) to logged-out users
findings.evidence:
temple.service.ts findAll select includes trustScore and orders by it:
  select: { ... isVerified: true, trustScore: true, liveDarshanEnabled: true },   // line 100
  orderBy: [{ trustScore: 'desc' }, { name: 'asc' }],                            // line 103

findNearby raw SQL selects trust_score and maps it through:
  SELECT id, name, name_local, slug, deity_primary, tradition, city, state, lat, lng, images, is_verified, trust_score, live_darshan_enabled, (...) AS distance_km FROM temples WHERE status='active' ...  // line 211
  trustScore: t.trust_score,   // line 246 (returned to client)

search select also includes trustScore:
  select: { ... isVerified: true, trustScore: true, liveDarshanEnabled: true },   // line 287
  orderBy: [{ trustScore: 'desc' }, { name: 'asc' }],                            // line 290

findBySlug (detail) uses findUnique with `include` and NO top-level `select` -> returns the FULL Temple row:
  const temple = await prisma.temple.findUnique({ where: { slug }, include: { priests: {...}, pujaOfferings: {...}, darshanStream: {...} } });  // lines 125-174

Temple schema has private/internal columns beyond trustScore:
  phone String?  email String?  streamUrl String? @map("stream_url")  status TempleStatus @default(pending_review)  verificationDate DateTime?  // schema.prisma:260,261,269,270,266

Web client TempleDetail type confirms these are consumed publicly:
  export interface TempleDetail extends TempleListItem { ... phone: string|null; email: string|null; ... streamUrl: string|null; verificationDate: string|null; }  // apps/web/lib/api.ts:113-122

All four temple routes are unauthenticated:
  server.get('/', ...)        // temples.ts:6
  server.get('/search', ...)  // temples.ts:41
  server.get('/nearby', ...)  // temples.ts:63
  server.get('/:slug', ...)   // temples.ts:102
findings.impact: trustScore is an internal ranking/moderation signal (not a user-facing rating) — exposing it leaks the ranking algorithm inputs and lets providers game their placement; ordering by it publicly confirms which temples the platform considers low-trust. The DETAIL endpoint (/temples/:slug) is worse: findBySlug returns the full row including phone, email (temple contact PII), streamUrl (could be a private RTMP ingest key rather than a public YouTube embed), status (pending_review/active internal moderation state), and verificationDate. A pending_review or rejected temple whose slug is known can be fully read by a logged-out user via /:slug (findBySlug has no status='active' filter, unlike findAll/search/nearby).
findings.repro: curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/temples' -> each item has trustScore. curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/temples/<slug>' -> response.temple contains phone, email, streamUrl, status, verificationDate, trustScore.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove trustScore from all four public selects (or replace with a derived 0-5 `rating` band if user-facing signal is desired). In findBySlug, replace `include`-only with an explicit top-level `select` that excludes phone/email/streamUrl/status/verificationDate/trustScore, AND add a where clause filter for status='active' (return 404 for pending_review/rejected temples) so unapproved temples aren't publicly readable by slug.

findings.title: /api/v1/admin/cron/tick still accepts cron token as ?token= query param (legacy fallback) -> leaks secret into Render access logs + CDN caches
findings.impact: PARTIAL fix since the prior audit: the timing-safe compare (timingSafeEqual) was added, closing the timing-oracle half of the original finding. However the query-param leak vector remains: a caller can still pass ?token=<CRON_AUTH_TOKEN> and it will be accepted. Query strings are logged verbatim in Render access logs, CDN/edge logs, and any upstream proxy logs, and may be cached by intermediary caches — so the cron secret can be disclosed via log access or cache exposure. The header path is safe; the query fallback is the residual risk.
findings.repro: curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/admin/cron/tick?token=<SECRET>' -> 200 + runDailyOps() output. The secret now appears in the Render access log line for that request.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the queryToken fallback entirely (accept x-cron-token header only). If an external free-tier pinger (UptimeRobot) cannot send headers, front it with a thin redirect/relay that injects the header, or rotate to a dedicated low-privilege token for the query path. At minimum, configure Render/CDN to strip/scrub the token query param from access logs and set Cache-Control: no-store on the response (currently none set).

findings.title: /api/v1/astrology/horoscope/prewarm compares cron secret with plain !== (timing oracle) AND skips auth entirely when CRON_SECRET env is unset (default-allow)
findings.impact: Two distinct problems vs the cron-auth middleware doctrine. (1) Timing oracle: `token !== cronSecret` (line 204) is a short-circuiting string compare that leaks the secret byte-by-byte via response timing, unlike the constant-time compare used everywhere else (cron-auth.ts, and the admin-leads tick handler that was hardened in PUB-03). (2) Default-allow: the `if (cronSecret)` guard (line 202) means if CRON_SECRET is missing/empty in any environment (misconfigured deploy, a Render env var that didn't propagate, a test/staging instance), the auth check is SKIPPED entirely and prewarmDailyHoroscopes() runs for ANY anonymous caller — the opposite of cron-auth's fail-loud default-deny. prewarmDailyHoroscopes likely fans out 12+ LLM/astrology computations (a cost/abuse vector, not just a data leak).
findings.repro: If CRON_SECRET is unset on the instance: curl -X POST 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/astrology/horoscope/prewarm' (no headers) -> 200 { prewarmed: ... }. Timing attack: send repeated requests with progressively-correct token prefixes and measure response time differences (plain !== short-circuits on first differing byte).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the handler with the existing requireCronBearer middleware (or requireCronQueryToken) from middlewares/cron-auth.ts — it already implements constant-time compare AND default-deny (401 cron_auth_misconfigured when env unset). Add `{ preHandler: [requireCronBearer] }` to the route and delete the inline check. Ensure CRON_SECRET is set in every deployed environment.

findings.title: Mobile /profile renders a fake hardcoded user profile (name + phone + stats + Sign Out) to logged-out visitors with no auth gate
findings.evidence:
export default function MobileProfile() { // line 34 — 'use client' component, no useSession/auth check, no redirect ...

Arjun Sharma

// line 44 — hardcoded fake name

+91 98765 43210

// line 45 — hardcoded fake phone (PII-shaped) ... Bhakti Pass Member since 2026 // lines 47-51 — fake subscription/tier ...

12

Bookings

...

3

Temples

...

₹8.5K

Spent

// lines 60-72 — fake spend/bookings stats ... // line 127 — functional-looking sign-out with no session
findings.impact: A logged-out visitor to /mobile/profile sees a fully populated profile (name, phone number, subscription tier, booking count, total spend) and an editable 'Edit' button + 'Sign Out' button — presenting as if logged in. No real PII leak (data is fake), but: (a) misleading UX / placeholder shipped to prod, (b) the fake phone number '+91 98765 43210' is a real-format Indian mobile that could be misinterpreted as a real user's, (c) no auth gate means the page never redirects to sign-in, masking the fact that the mobile app shell has no real session wiring here. Compounding: /mobile home page (mobile/page.tsx:38) also greets 'Arjun Sharma' hardcoded.
findings.repro: Open https://darshya.online/mobile/profile in a clean browser (no cookies) -> full fake profile renders, no login redirect.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an auth gate: useSession()/auth context check that redirects to /sign-in when unauthenticated, OR render an empty-state 'Sign in to view your profile' CTA. Replace all hardcoded PII with real session data once wired. Same for the /mobile home greeting.

findings.title: NEW: /api/v1/semantic-search leaks unpublished/draft temples and content (no status filter) — unlike /api/v1/search and /api/v1/content which correctly filter
findings.evidence:
Vector path — raw SQL has NO status/isActive filter, scans every row with an embedding:
  select id, ${titleColSql} as title, coalesce(left(${snippetColSql}, 240), '') as snippet, 1 - (embedding <=> ${lit}::vector) as score
    from ${tableSql}
   where embedding is not null
   order by embedding <=> ${lit}::vector
   limit ${lim}   // lines 66-74 — no `where status='active'`/`status='published'`

LIKE fallback path — also no status filter on any of the three tables:
  prisma.contentItem.findMany({ where: { OR: [{ title: { contains: q, mode: 'insensitive' } }, { body: { contains: q, mode: 'insensitive' } }] }, select: {...}, take: limit })  // lines 89-94 — NO status:'published'
  prisma.temple.findMany({ where: { OR: [{ name: {...} }, { description: {...} }] }, select: {...}, take: limit })  // lines 108-113 — NO status:'active'
  prisma.pujaType.findMany({ where: { OR: [{ name: {...} }, { description: {...} }] }, select: {...}, take: limit })  // lines 127-132 — NO isActive filter

Compare the CORRECT pattern in /api/v1/search (search.ts):
  prisma.temple.findMany({ where: { OR: [...], status: 'active' }, ... })        // search.ts:33
  prisma.contentItem.findMany({ where: { OR: [...], status: 'published' }, ... }) // search.ts:73

And content.service.ts:
  const where = { status: 'published', ... }   // content.service.ts:30,198 ; findBySlug: if (!item || item.status !== 'published') return null // line 104
findings.impact: Logged-out users can discover pending_review temples, draft/unpublished content items, and inactive puja types via /api/v1/semantic-search — entities that are correctly hidden from /api/v1/search and /api/v1/content. A draft blog/article exposing unreleased features, a pending_review temple with unverified/PII-laden description, or a deactivated puja can all be surfaced by semantic query. This is an inconsistency that turns the semantic endpoint into a draft-content oracle. Secondary: the vector path calls generateEmbedding() (a Cohere API billable call) on every request with only the global 100/min/IP rate limit (no tightened per-route cap in server.ts:162-181 for /semantic-search), so anonymous abuse drives LLM spend.
findings.repro: curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/semantic-search?q=<term-matching-a-draft>&kind=all' -> hits include draft content_items (status<>'published') and pending_review temples (status<>'active') that /api/v1/search?q=<same> correctly excludes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add status filters to BOTH paths in semantic-search.ts: vector path -> append `and status='active'` (temples) / `status='published'` (content_items) / `is_active=true` (puja_types) to the raw SQL per table (requires per-table SQL branch since columns differ); LIKE fallback -> add `status: 'published'`/`status: 'active'`/`isActive: true` to each findMany where. Also add a tightened rate-limit policy for url.startsWith('/semantic-search') in server.ts onRoute hook (e.g. max: 20/min) to cap embedding API spend.

findings.title: NEW: /api/v1/providers/:type/:id detail endpoint bypasses the approved-gate — returns full row of UNAPPROVED providers by UUID
findings.evidence:
queryProviderById uses findUnique by id only — no approved filter, no select:
  case 'pandit': return (await prisma.panditProfile.findUnique({ where: { id } })) as unknown as Record<string, unknown> | null;  // line 454
  case 'store':  return (await prisma.storeProfile.findUnique({ where: { id } })) ...   // line 456
  ... (same for astrologer/wellness/gaushala/temple, lines 457-464)

getProviderById passes the raw row through enrichRatingFields (which spreads ...p, see PUB-01) and returns it:
  const provider = await this.queryProviderById(type, id);   // line 239
  ... const enriched = await this.enrichRatingFields(type, provider); return { ...enriched, reviews };  // lines 258-259

Contrast with the LIST queryProviders which DOES gate on approved:
  const where: Record<string, unknown> = { approved: true };   // line 327
findings.impact: The list endpoint hides unapproved providers (where approved:true), but the detail endpoint does not. An attacker who obtains any provider UUID (via a prior approved listing that leaked userId/id, a分享 link, an admin log, or brute-force/enumeration of UUIDs if predictable) can GET /providers/:type/:id and read the full PII row of a PENDING, REJECTED, or never-approved provider — including userId, gstNumber, commission, aadhaarVerified, availability, approved, approvedAt. This defeats the moderation gate for the detail view and exposes applicant PII that was never meant to be public. Combined with PUB-01 (no field projection), the detail endpoint is the worst single endpoint in the provider surface.
findings.repro: Obtain a pandit profile UUID known to have approved=false (e.g. from a test signup). curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/providers/pandit/<uuid>' (no auth) -> 200 with full row including approved:false, userId, aadhaarVerified, availability.
findings.suggestedFix: In queryProviderById, switch from findUnique({where:{id}}) to findFirst({where:{id, approved:true}}) for every type, and add an explicit `select` whitelist (exclude userId/gstNumber/commission/aadhaarVerified/availability/approved/approvedAt). Return null (-> route 404) for unapproved ids. This single change closes both PUB-01's field leak and PUB-07's gate bypass on the detail endpoint.

findings.title: NEW: /api/v1/temples/:slug detail returns full Temple row incl. phone, email, streamUrl, status, verificationDate to logged-out users (no status='active' gate)
findings.evidence:
findBySlug uses findUnique with `include` only — no top-level `select`, no status filter:
  const temple = await prisma.temple.findUnique({
    where: { slug },
    include: { priests: { include: { priest: { select: {...} } }, orderBy: { isPrimary: 'desc' } }, pujaOfferings: {...}, darshanStream: {...} },
  });   // lines 125-174 — the Temple row itself is unprojected

Temple schema private columns returned:
  phone String?  email String?  websiteUrl String?  streamUrl String? @map("stream_url")  status TempleStatus @default(pending_review)  verificationDate DateTime?  // schema.prisma:260-266

The route returns it raw to anonymous callers:
  server.get('/:slug', async (request, reply) => { ... const temple = await templeService.findBySlug(slug); if (!temple) return reply.status(404)... return { temple }; });  // temples.ts:102-117
findings.impact: A logged-out user can read temple contact PII (phone, email), the streamUrl (which may be a private RTMP ingest key for self-streaming temples rather than a public YouTube embed — exposing it would let anyone hijack/inject the stream), internal moderation state (status: pending_review/active, verificationDate), and trustScore. Unlike findAll/search/nearby which filter status='active', findBySlug has NO status filter, so a pending_review or rejected temple is fully readable by slug — leaking unverified/unapproved temple data and any PII its submitter entered. (The priests include DOES use a safe select that excludes commissionRate/certificationDocs/aadhaarVerified/verificationStatus — that part is fine.)
findings.suggestedFix: In findBySlug, add a top-level `select` to the findUnique that whitelists only public columns (id, name, nameLocal, slug, description, deityPrimary, deities, tradition, addressLine, city, state, pincode, country, lat, lng, websiteUrl, images, timingInfo, isVerified, liveDarshanEnabled) and excludes phone, email, streamUrl, status, verificationDate, trustScore, embedding. Additionally filter by status='active' (use findFirst with where:{slug, status:'active'}) so unapproved temples 404.

findings.title: REFUTED areas: CORS not wildcard, global rate-limit present, /users not public, error pages no stack trace, sitemap/robots exclude admin, search/content filter drafts, priests-public is projected, provider-kyc auth-gated + masked, astrology SEO pages guarded (noted for completeness)

findings.impact: No vulnerability — documents the checked-and-clean surfaces so the caller knows they were audited, not skipped. The one residual in server.ts: the onRoute rate-limit hook (162-181) adds no tightened policy for /providers/, /temples/, /content/, /search/, /semantic-search/ — these expensive public listing/search endpoints run under the global 100/min/IP default. Not a leak, but a cost/abuse surface (esp. /semantic-search which triggers Cohere embedding calls — see PUB-06).
findings.suggestedFix: Optional hardening: add tightened per-route rate caps for /semantic-search and /search (e.g. max: 20/min) in the server.ts onRoute hook to cap LLM/DB spend on anonymous traffic. No action needed for the rest.

summary.topFinding: PUB-01 / PUB-07 (provider endpoints): public /api/v1/providers/:type and /:type/:id return FULL DB rows (userId, GST, commission, aadhaarVerified, availability) to logged-out users, and the detail endpoint additionally bypasses the approved-gate so UNAPPROVED provider PII is readable by UUID — both confirmed and worse than originally filed.
